newsitem.title: USA: Texaco says Lundwall acted against company policy.
newsitem.headline: Texaco says Lundwall acted against company policy.

text.p: Texaco Inc said Tuesday that Richard Lundwall, the former company executive charged with obstruction of justice, was acting against company policy by allegedly destroying documents related to a racial bias suit.

Lundwall was charged in a New York District Court on Tuesday with obstructing justice, arising from a civil lawsuit brought against Texaco by a group of black employees alleging racial discrimination.

"If Mr Lundwall did what he was charged with, he was acting in direct violation of expressed company policy as well as written instructions from the company's general consul to preserve all documents relating to the discrimination lawsuit," said company spokesman James Swords.
Lundwall, a former senior coordinator of personnel services in Texaco's financial department, allegedly shredded and concealed documents critical to the lawsuit, according to court papers.
Texaco reached a settlement for an estimated $176 million in the racial discrimination suit last Friday.
"Texaco is cooperating fully with the U.S. attorney in this investigation," Swords said, adding the company had no further comment.
